unreg:draft_selection.rederivation_notes: Written before reading the record: chain = lottery (2 weighted draws, max 10-spot rise, no club wins more than twice in 5 years under the 2021/2022 rules) sets slots 1-16 among non-playoff clubs; slots 17-32 are set by playoff round of elimination (then regular-season points; Cup winner 32nd), so for slot contracts beyond 16 the playoff outcome distribution is an input. Pick-ownership ledger (trades, conditional/protected picks, forfeitures, draft-day trades) maps slot to selecting club. Holder picks sequentially from a board (Central Scouting, McKenzie/TSN, Elite Prospects, others) modulated by need, staff habit, combine medicals, insider reports; pick k is conditional on picks 1..k-1 (depletion cascade, Plackett-Luce-type joint simulation). Hazards: player vs club vs slot basis, pick traded before the call, eligibility cut-off, forfeited slot shifting order, decentralised draft timing (2025+), no rules text. After comparing: the author covers lottery, ownership, board, need, GM habit, medical, insider and trade hazard well and honestly flags no rules text, but (a) ignores the playoff-determined slots 17-32 and mis-states that playoff clubs do not hold their own slot, (b) adds draft_board_dispersion and uses reference_class_hazard for a calibration the existing prospect_consensus_ranking already defines, (c) has no explicit sequential-depletion structure, and (d) relies on CapFriendly and multi-service ranking archives back to 2005 that likely do not exist in usable form.

findings.text: Missing mechanism and input for slots 17-32. Stage s1 says 'Final regular-season standings ... determine' the order and 'Clubs that make the playoffs ... do not hold their own slot'. That is wrong: playoff clubs hold slots 17-32, ordered by playoff round of elimination (Cup winner picks 32nd, finalist 31st), with regular-season points used only within a group. A 'Pro Hockey Draft Pick' contract on any slot above 16, or on which club picks there, needs a playoff-round outcome distribution, for example a series/bracket simulation using nhl.ratings, nhl.bracket_path_difficulty and nhl.series_context. nhl.season_sim_distribution covers points and qualification, not round of elimination. No such input is listed.

Duplicate inputs. The existing catalog input nhl.prospect_consensus_ranking already measures 'gap between first and second' and calibrates 'P(consensus #1 is selected first) ... for later picks use rank deviation distributions ... update with injuries and with team-specific needs flags'. The new nhl.draft_board_dispersion (cross-service SD, k vs k+1 gap, 'historical frequency that the consensus rank-k prospect went exactly at slot k') repeats that calibration. nhl.reference_class_hazard (role 'base rate that the consensus first-ranked prospect goes first overall') repeats it a third time. The interaction 'prospect_consensus_ranking x draft_board_dispersion' therefore describes the inside of one input, not an interaction between two. Either narrow prospect_consensus_ranking's definition or drop or merge the new id, and remove reference_class_hazard.

There is no stage, interaction or nonlinearity for sequential depletion: the distribution at slot k depends on which prospects were taken at slots 1..k-1. The measurement for draft_board_dispersion calibrates on the unconditional 'rank-k prospect went exactly at slot k'. That is the wrong target once an earlier reach occurs, because a single off-board pick shifts every later slot by one. Slot contracts need a joint, conditional-on-remaining-board model (e.g. a conditional logit over the remaining prospects, which interaction 3's how_to_test mentions only in passing), with the full board as required data, not just the slot in question.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED and likely wrong. (a) CapFriendly is cited as a free source ('CapFriendly archive' for pick ownership; CapFriendly/PuckPedia for contract expiries), but it shut down in July 2024 after the Washington Capitals acquired it; only Wayback snapshots remain. The record's own note ('site status should be confirmed') is not carried into unresolved. (b) draft_board_dispersion needs ranks from '>=4 independent services' per prospect 'pooled 2005-present'. Of the named services, McKeen's and FC Hockey are largely paywalled, Elite Prospects' draft-guide rankings are paid, and public archives of the McKenzie list before about 2010 are patchy. A 2005-present multi-service history is very likely unavailable, which changes the calibration window. Neither gap is in unresolved.

Irrelevant inputs are kept in catalog_entry.inputs despite the author's own WEAK verdicts. nhl.career_trajectory (built for NHL age curves) and nhl.offfield_base_rate ('draft happening on schedule is near-certain') are still listed as context. required_data also maps them to unrelated datasets: career_trajectory to 'Public prospect rankings', offfield_base_rate to the 'medical and eligibility log and insider reports'. Drop both, or justify them.

Prospect production (junior/NCAA/European scoring, NHL-equivalency) and combine testing are not inputs. They are absorbed into consensus rankings, which is acceptable for slot 1 but not for slots where clubs deviate from consensus. Also, the input_audit silently drops the blueprint inputs award_stats, award_voting_rules, ratings, goalie_quality and injuries_pit without a verdict.

The interaction gm_draft_behavior_history x insider_report_credibility (form 'multiplicative') is asserted without support, and it cannot be back-tested: insider-report history is 'own_capture' with 'no clean public archive', so 'several drafts of reports' do not exist yet. Disclose this as DATA_UNAVAILABLE.

Wording and history. history_needed says 'weighted lottery since 1995 with modifications since 2013, 2021'. It omits the 2016 three-draw format and the 2022 limit of two wins in five years, which the mechanism refers to as 'win limits'. Settlement edge cases omit the decentralised draft format (2025 onward) and the case where a selected player's rights are later renounced or voided. Settlement itself is correctly marked NOT_VERIFIED_NO_RULES_TEXT, and no verbatim claims were made.

unreg:playoff_series_aggregate.rederivation_notes: Written before reading the record: total = sum over N in {4..7} games. N comes from per-game win probabilities with the 2-2-1-1-1 home pattern; E[N] is about 5.81 at parity. Playoff games have no shootout and end on sudden-death 5v5 OT, so if OT goals count, an OT game adds exactly one goal, total = even regulation total + 1, and the number of OT periods does not affect goals. The key per-game quantity is P(regulation tie) (catalog nhl.reg_tie_model). Per-game mean comes from xGF/xGA, goalie quality and the confirmed starter, the playoff environment (fewer PPs), empty-net goals in close games and series state. Variance of the sum is driven by game-level overdispersion plus a series-level shared shock in matchup scoring rate (rating/scoring uncertainty), which scales with N^2. A series-level win-probability shock makes series more lopsided (more sweeps, fewer 7-game series), not longer. Hazards: OT inclusion, unfinished or postponed series, source of truth, half-goal strikes, market opening mid-series. After comparing: the structure (random-length compound sum, joint length/goal mean, live state) matches, and settlement is honestly marked unverified. But the record states the wrong sign for within-series dependence on length, models OT period length although goals per OT game are fixed at one, invents an OT input that duplicates catalog ids while ignoring nhl.reg_tie_model and nhl.series_ot_count_dependence, and has no series-level shared scoring-rate uncertainty input (nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty).

findings.text: Wrong mechanism sign. Stage s2 says 'Series are positively correlated through goaltending runs, so seven-game tails are thicker than binomial'. The series_game_count_pmf rationale says correlation 'fattens the 7-game tail', and its measurement applies 'a common series-level shock to the log-odds'. A common shock spreads the effective p away from 0.5, and E[N] and P(N=7) are concave and maximal at parity, so this shortens series (more sweeps, fewer 7-game series). A thicker 7-game tail requires negative dependence (bounce-back, home-ice alternation). The sign changes the length pmf and the total's mean. Re-derive this, and test both directions against the historical 7-game share.

nhl.playoff_ot_length_distribution is mis-specified. With sudden death, every completed OT game adds exactly one goal regardless of the number of periods. Yet the record says OT adds 'possibly several periods of events', 'Overtime periods add goals and games in the sum' (OT adds no games), and the nonlinearity says the geometric period tail makes 'the contribution of long games to the sum ... small but not negligible'. Period count is irrelevant to series total goals. Only P(regulation tie) and the counting convention matter. The input also duplicates existing catalog ids nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5 (playoff 5v5 OT hazard) and nhl.series_ot_count_dependence (within-series dependence of OT occurrence, beta-binomial), neither of which is used or audited.

Missing existing inputs that change the data required. (a) nhl.reg_tie_model (regulation tie probability) is the actual driver of how often a game total is forced odd and gains an OT goal. The record's OT stage has no tie-probability input. (b) nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty: uncertainty in the pair's scoring rate is shared by all games, so it adds variance to the sum that grows with N^2. total_goal_dispersion is per-game, and series_goalie_volatility covers only goaltending. Without this the over/under tails are understated. (c) nhl.goalie_start_forecast and nhl.rest_travel: playoff starter changes and rest days (from 1 to 3+ days between games) vary within a series and are not covered by goalie_quality.

nhl.series_game_count_pmf is not an input but a derived model output of ratings, goalie, injuries and venue (its measurement computes it 'from team ratings, goalie, injuries and venue'). Listing it as primary alongside nhl.ratings and nhl.goalie_quality double-counts the same information. The interaction 'ratings x series_game_count_pmf' is then a functional dependency, not an interaction between independent inputs. Label it as a model output (as the catalog does for nhl.pair_difference_distribution) or fold it into the simulation, and keep only the dependence parameter as data.

The interaction goalie_quality x series_goalie_volatility claims a hot or cold streak 'shifts both the number of games and the goals per game in the same direction'. That holds only for the favourite's goalie. A hot underdog goalie lowers goals per game and lengthens the series, so the directions are opposite. The interaction exists, but its stated form is wrong.

nhl.empty_net is used alongside nhl.total_goal_dispersion, whose catalog label already says 'incl. empty-net contribution', so there is a double-counting risk. The blueprint inputs pdo_regression, news, sos_remaining, standings_tiebreakers and m.external_lines are dropped with no input_audit verdict (dropping m.external_lines is correct). injuries_pit is placed in stage s4 'Overtime periods and settlement counting', where it has no role.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: the 'Daily Faceoff line archives' are cited as a source for line combos back to 2010 (series_adjustment_regime). A historical archive is doubtful. Line combinations should be derived from NHL shift charts instead. Daily Faceoff starter confirmations have 'no clean archive', but historical starters are available from NHL API boxscores, so that dependency is unnecessary for back-tests.

Settlement is correctly marked NOT_VERIFIED_NO_RULES_TEXT and makes no verbatim claims. The 'about a fifth of games' OT share and 'about 5.8 games at parity' (exact 5.8125 under iid) are consistent. One gap: there is no edge case for a market listed mid-series, where goals already scored count toward the strike. series_context mentions 'goals already banked' but required_data does not timestamp per-game totals against market open.
